reviews.title: Another amazing product from Thermalright
reviews.comment: Thermalright has been building top notch stuff and I love that they came out with a case with such a good look. The build quality on this is a punch above the rest with how thick the metal panels are, how spacious and ease of assembly is. Temps seem to be solid too. For the price, its a great value as it comes with a nice loooooong screen that has a metal casing around it, but no fans..a bit of a bummer it has none at all, but its to be expected at this price range and level of case. Overall building in it was perfectly fine, tons of room to hide cables. A bit annoying clipping all the mix matched colored bread ties in the back but minor complaints comapred to how good this looks.

reviews.title: Awesome case, worth the money
reviews.comment: Very easy to work in, I didnt even bother to take all the glass panels off. Perfect size, bigger than what I had and was a little cramped so not too big, not too small. Sturdy, and high quality. The magnetic screen does slide down alot but the lian li lcd fans are pretty girthy so they rest up against the metal aio cover so its probably just vibrations. Easy fix with some double sided tape. I love it.
reviews.author: Vinny

reviews.title: Fantastic PC Case – Thermalright built a Banger!
reviews.comment: Thermalright making a PC case? LOL I didn’t expect it either. But here we are… and it’s honestly one of the best I’ve used. First, the everyday stuff: This case is gorgeous. Clean, modern, and just looks right sitting on a desk. It’s also incredibly easy to work with. Disassembly is simple, everything is accessible, and the overall build process is smooth. This is one of those cases that actually makes building a PC enjoyable instead of feeling like a chore. Now, the negatives (and I’m stretching a bit here): 1. PSU Clearance Issue I checked compatibility using Rufus for my MSI PRO Z890-S WIFI PZ motherboard, and visually everything looked fine. And technically, it is… but the PSU opening caused a problem. My power supply cables couldn’t properly connect to the motherboard. That’s not something you want to force or “make work.” It’s a small issue, but important. I’d call it a 1% flaw on an otherwise near-perfect case. 2. Grommet Placement The side grommets can interfere with rear-connect motherboards. Not a dealbreaker, but something to be aware of depending on your setup. I’ve built around 40 PCs in the past year, using a wide range of cases. This one? It beats all of them. Don't pass on this case. Thank you Thermalright!
reviews.author: Crush Bowman
